Review: clean (safety tier, read only, not built by this reviewer).

Head 4664df470 merges cleanly with `main` (MERGEABLE, CLEAN).

Checks:

1. Post order. `fanuc.cps` `xyFirst` sends `G00 Z<tz>`, then `G00 X Y`, then the move with the rotary words. When the first rapid is already at the clearance, X/Y and the rotary words go in one block, so the work also passes through poses between the old and new angles. A full turn and a full sphere contain those poses. The premise (the start is at the tool-change height) is stated in decision item 1 and under "Not exercised" in the PR body.
2. Swept set. Each rotary line goes through the WCS origin. Then each composed turn is a turn about that origin and keeps the distance from it, so the sphere is an upper bound. A full circle about one line is an upper bound for one rotary. The distance to a point or to a line is convex, so the corner read of a box is exact. A fixture that does not ride the rotary is also read high, never low: each point lies on its own circle or sphere. A rotary line that does not go through the WCS origin is not refused. It is read as if it went through the origin. The decision file states this limit ("Known limits", item 2), and the index-swing clause (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs` lines 28-40) has the same premise. No shipped machine file states `pivot` or `offset`. This is not a blocker for this PR. A refusal when a machine states a pivot or offset that is not zero is a possible follow-up.
3. A lone tilting work-turning rotary with no usable line (`RotaryLine::Unknown`, or `Leaning` with no stated axis) refuses by name (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse_posed.rs:79-83`). `a_work_turning_rotary_with_no_line_refuses_by_name` pins the text.
4. The `retain` removes only `FirstTraverseLow` verdicts that have a lower top (`first_traverse_posed.rs:126`). `FirstTraverseUnderTable` and all other kinds stay. The one verdict that stays names the highest top, so the repair (raise the clearance) also clears the removed ones.
5. Traverse height. For the non-rotary kinds it is `max(clearance, move 0 height)`, which agrees with `traverseZ`. For the rotary kinds it is the clearance alone, because move 0 is a radial pose. This agrees with the #2965 reading. With no finite clearance it uses move 0, and the post then refuses the traverse by itself.
6. The new law is proven on its own. The app pins read the cached warnings and assert `FirstTraverseLow` with `top_mm` equal to sqrt(354) = 18.815 (the fitted-axis law reads 9.899) and sqrt(544) = 23.324 (the part frame reads 12). They also assert exactly one such verdict, and that clearance 20 / 25 gives no verdict. These values come only from the new law. Only the post refusal is checked with `is_err`, and that is acceptable.
7. Other checks:
   - The stamp word `first-traverse-posed-3084` is added only when `turn_of` is not `Ok(None)`.
   - The PR changes no shipped post, machine file or example project.
   - There is no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests, and no check is made weaker.
   - `first_traverse::judge` does not change.

Notes (not blockers):
- `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs` has 404 lines, which is about the 400-line limit. Split it at the next change that adds lines.
- 3+2 operations and the cross drill on a work-tilting machine are not judged by this law. The follow-up is #3100.

Gate: I relied on the worker's local debug runs on this head (sim `first_traverse` 12; app `first_traverse_posed` 3, `first_traverse_rotary`, `first_traverse_table`, `rotary_contour_x`, `microarc_test_part`, `index_swing`, `setup_align_multiaxis`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_4axis_part`, `example_catalog`; clippy sim and app clean). Heavy lanes: not run. This is not a pass. The P1 stack batch gate and the cut gate must cover them.

Branch refresh. The new head is 0f9b05f27.

- 81cc1b6c5 merges #3122 (0172bb464). One hunk conflicted in `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`. The resolution keeps both stamp words, each with its own condition, in the order of main: `live-traverse-rotary-3096`, then `first-traverse-posed-3084`. `generate.rs` and `operation/mod.rs` merged with no conflict.
- 8cf7230cf is new code. #3096 adds `rotary_traverse::mill_post_rotary` to `mill_order` in `generate.rs`. Thus the posed law can read a rotary kind on a mill-turn. The stamp cannot read the path. Now `first_traverse_posed::newly_judged` reads each mill and mill-turn setup in the mill order. One extra word only makes a cache Stale one time.
- 0f9b05f27 merges `origin/main` (404f8ec46, which contains #3122). There is no conflict and no hand hunk: `git show --remerge-diff` is empty. Against main, the diff is the 8 files of this PR only.
- The P1 stack gate ran on 8cf7230cf (main + #3122 + #3125). Result: batch 1027 steps, 0 failed. The light lane is green.
- 0 CR bytes in each changed blob.

Delta review: clean

Base of this review: the clean Opus review on 4664df470 (comment 7060737872). This review reads the three commits after it. No build: read-only delta review.

- `81cc1b6c5` (merge of #3122 `0172bb464`), class DELTA. `git show --remerge-diff` has one hunk in `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`. The resolution keeps the two stamp words: `live-traverse-rotary-3096`, then `first-traverse-posed-3084`. Each word keeps its own condition. Nothing of the two sides is lost.
- `8cf7230cf`, class NEW CODE. `first_traverse_posed::newly_judged` now sets `mill` for each `Kind::Mill` and `Kind::MillTurn` setup.
  - Necessary: `generate.rs` now gives `turn_of` the value `mill_order || rotary_traverse::mill_post_rotary(...)`. `mill_post_rotary` reads the path (no `rotary` word on the moves). The stamp cannot read the path. With the old `mill_order(kind, false, params)` alone, an unstamped rotary kind on a mill-turn got the posed law in `generate` but no `first-traverse-posed-3084` word. That cache stayed fresh without the posed verdict.
  - Sufficient: the `mill_order` of `generate` is true only on `Mill` or `MillTurn` (`first_traverse::mill_order` and `mill_post_rotary` both require one of the two). `turn_of` returns `Ok(None)` when `mill` is false. Otherwise its result depends only on `params` and the rotaries. The stamp reads the same machine rotaries: `job.machine_rotaries` comes from the mounted machine of the setup, and `work_turning` filters `rotary` again. The stamp `wcs_origin` of `[0.0; 3]` does not change `Ok(None)` against `Some`/`Err`. Thus each operation that the posed law reads gets the word.
  - Extra words: a lathe tool or a stamped rotary kind on a mill-turn now gets the word but no posed verdict. The result is only one Stale read. This is the safe direction, and the commit message and the doc comment say so.
  - I found no case that the stamp still misses.
- `0f9b05f27` (merge of main `404f8ec46`), class SAME. `git show --remerge-diff` is empty.

Scope: `git diff origin/main...0f9b05f27` has only the 8 files of this PR (589 insertions, 1 deletion). Main `404f8ec46` contains #3122, and the stamp on the head keeps its `#3096` word. Nothing of #3122 is lost.

Gate (reported by the coordinator): the P1 stack batch on `8cf7230cf` (main + #3125 + #3122, Windows) has 1027 steps, 0 failed, and the light lane is green. `0f9b05f27` adds only the newer commits of main.

Ready and merge: the coordinator flags head 0f9b05f27 ready and merges it. Gate: the P1 stack batch tier on 8cf7230cf (= main + #3122 + this PR, local, Windows): 1027 steps, 0 failed; the light tier is green. 0f9b05f27 adds only a clean merge of main.
